title: FieldFox — a tiny field laboratory
purpose: Reusable editorial and scrollytelling resources for design review; not a launched product website.
lead: From the information you have to the form you need.
visualMetaphor: A friendly tabletop sorting device, annotated like an engineering drawing. The device stands for the whole workflow, never an on-device AI claim.

chapters.label: Gather
chapters.headline: Bring the bits you already have.
chapters.body: A message. A labelled photo. A supplier sheet. Give FieldFox the source beside the form you already use.
chapters.technical: Text and images are supported inputs. Enable document attachments with accept-documents; extraction depends on the chosen model.
chapters.motion: A folded source sheet and two small information tiles settle into the intake tray. Keep the source visible throughout.
chapters.alt: A source sheet with a product SKU, material and dimensions sits beside an empty product form.

chapters.label: Map
chapters.headline: Meet the little boxes.
chapters.body: FieldFox reads your form’s labels and supported controls. You can add hints and mark a field hands-off.
chapters.technical: The widget builds a form schema. data-ff-ignore excludes a field or subtree from introspection and filling.
chapters.motion: A cobalt frame follows each supported field; a dotted boundary steps around the manual-note field.
chapters.alt: The form becomes a labelled map. A separate internal-note field stays outside the map.

chapters.label: Propose
chapters.headline: Ask for a plan.
chapters.body: The source and the form map travel to your configured server and model provider. The model proposes where the information belongs.
chapters.technical: Browser → FieldFox server → compatible provider. Site-author guidance is separated from source content; the server validates the proposed fill plan.
chapters.motion: One visible packet crosses the browser boundary, enters the server, reaches the provider and returns through the plan-validation gate.
chapters.alt: Source and schema leave the browser for the server and model provider. A proposed plan returns to the server for validation.

chapters.label: Check
chapters.headline: Did it land in the box?
chapters.body: FieldFox applies supported values, then reads the fields back. That checks the write—not whether the source was understood correctly.
chapters.technical: Skipped and omitted fields stay as they were. A failed confirmation triggers a restore attempt for that field. Cancellation is not an all-or-nothing rollback.
chapters.motion: Three value tiles settle into matching fields. A small readback loop visits each field. Weight remains empty; the manual note does not move.
chapters.alt: SKU, material and dimensions are filled, then read back. Weight remains empty and the excluded manual note is preserved.

chapters.label: Review
chapters.headline: Your eyes. Your next move.
chapters.body: Compare the filled values with the source. Correct what needs correcting. FieldFox never submits the form.
chapters.technical: The widget reports its result. Your application keeps its own validation and submission flow. A readback match is not factual proof.
chapters.motion: The camera eases back to show the source and filled form side by side. A human review marker arrives; no submit animation plays.
chapters.alt: A person compares the source with the filled form, edits a value and retains control of the next action.

chapters.label: Choose a home
chapters.headline: One fox. Two homes.
chapters.body: Cloud is the planned easy starting point. Or run the MIT widget and server yourself, with a compatible model provider.
chapters.technical: Cloud is pre-launch: a free first fill before signup is the intended experience. Self-hosting is available for evaluation. The widget and fill engine are shared.
chapters.motion: The same little fox device stays centered while two infrastructure trays slide into view: planned Cloud and self-hosted evaluation.
chapters.alt: An identical FieldFox widget connects to either pre-launch Cloud or a self-hosted server. Both use a configured model provider.

example.label: Illustrative product card; values are invented, not an extraction benchmark.
example.sourceText: Little stool. SKU STOOL-014. Material: wood. Width: 32 cm. Depth: 32 cm. Height: 45 cm.

motionRules: The source, outbound request and human review must remain understandable without animation.
Reduced motion uses the same chapter order with static states; no forced camera travel.
Never animate a submit, guaranteed accuracy badge, private/local processing claim, or security certification.
Do not animate a skipped field as a failed fact check; the distinction is whether a write was attempted.
